title_en: Law of the People's Republic of China on Soil and Water Conservation

articles.content_en: This Law is formulated for the purpose of preventing and controlling soil erosion, protecting and rationally utilizing soil and water resources, mitigating hazards from floods, droughts, wind and sand, improving ecological environment, and ensuring sustainable development of economy and society.

Any activity related to soil and water conservation conducted within the territory of the People's Republic of China shall comply with this Law.
For the purpose of this Law, "soil and water conservation" refers to the prevention and control measures taken against soil erosion caused by natural factors and human activities.

The work of soil and water conservation shall follow the policy of giving priority to prevention, protecting first, overall planning, comprehensive control, adapting measures to local conditions, highlighting key points, scientific management, and emphasizing effectiveness.

People's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen unified leadership over soil and water conservation work, incorporate soil and water conservation into their national economic and social development plans, allocate special funds for tasks identified in soil and water conservation plans, and organize implementation.
The State shall implement a target responsibility system for soil and water conservation and an assessment, reward and punishment system for local people's governments at all levels in key prevention areas and key control areas of soil erosion.

The water administrative department of the State Council shall be in charge of soil and water conservation nationwide.
The river basin management agencies (hereinafter referred to as river basin management agencies) established by the water administrative department of the State Council in major rivers and lakes designated by the State shall, within their jurisdiction, perform the supervision and management duties for soil and water conservation according to law.
The water administrative departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall be in charge of soil and water conservation within their respective administrative regions.
The relevant departments of forestry, agriculture, land and resources, etc., of people's governments at or above the county level shall, in accordance with their respective functions, properly carry out the prevention and control of soil erosion.

People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall strengthen publicity and education on soil and water conservation, popularize scientific knowledge of soil and water conservation, and enhance public awareness of soil and water conservation.

The State encourages and supports scientific and technological research on soil and water conservation, improves the level of science and technology in soil and water conservation, promotes advanced soil and water conservation technologies, and cultivates scientific and technological talents for soil and water conservation.

Any unit or individual has the obligation to protect soil and water resources, prevent and control soil erosion, and has the right to report any act that destroys soil and water resources or causes soil erosion.

The State encourages and supports social forces to participate in soil and water conservation work.
Units and individuals that have made remarkable achievements in soil and water conservation work shall be commended and rewarded by people's governments at or above the county level.

Soil and water conservation plans shall be formulated on the basis of soil erosion survey results and the delimitation of key prevention areas and key control areas for soil erosion, following the principles of overall coordination and classified guidance.

The water administrative department of the State Council shall regularly organize national soil erosion surveys and announce the survey results.
The water administrative departments of the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall be responsible for soil erosion surveys in their respective administrative regions and announce the survey results; before announcement, they shall report the survey results to the water administrative department of the State Council for record.

People's governments at or above the county level shall, based on soil erosion survey results, delimit and announce key prevention areas and key control areas for soil erosion.
Areas with relatively high potential danger of soil erosion shall be delimited as key prevention areas for soil erosion; areas with severe soil erosion shall be delimited as key control areas for soil erosion.

The contents of a soil and water conservation plan shall include the status of soil erosion, classification of soil erosion types, objectives, tasks, and measures for soil erosion prevention and control.
A soil and water conservation plan includes an overall deployment for the prevention and control of soil erosion and the protection and rational utilization of soil and water resources for a river basin or region, as well as special deployments for specific soil and water conservation work or for prevention and control of soil erosion in specific areas based on the overall deployment.
Soil and water conservation plans shall be coordinated with overall land use plans, water resource plans, urban and rural plans, and environmental protection plans.
When formulating a soil and water conservation plan, opinions of experts and the public shall be solicited.

The water administrative department of a people's government at or above the county level shall, jointly with the relevant departments of the same people's government, formulate a soil and water conservation plan, which shall be implemented by the water administrative department after being approved by the same people's government or its authorized department.
Once approved, a soil and water conservation plan shall be strictly implemented; if modification is necessary due to actual circumstances, it shall be submitted to the original approving authority for approval in accordance with the planning formulation procedures.

For plans concerning infrastructure construction, mineral resources development, urban construction, public service facility construction, etc., which may cause soil erosion during implementation, the organizing and formulating organs of the plans shall propose countermeasures and measures for soil erosion prevention and control in the plans, and solicit opinions from the water administrative department of the people's government at the same level before submitting the plans for approval.

Local people's governments at all levels shall, in accordance with soil and water conservation plans, adopt measures such as enclosure protection and natural restoration, organize units and individuals to plant trees and grass, expand forest and grass coverage, conserve water sources, and prevent and mitigate soil erosion.

Local people's governments at all levels shall strengthen the management of activities such as soil extraction, sand digging, and stone quarrying to prevent and mitigate soil erosion.
It is prohibited to engage in activities such as soil extraction, sand digging, and stone quarrying that may cause soil erosion in areas prone to collapse, landslide, and debris flow. The scope of areas prone to collapse, landslide, and debris flow shall be delimited and announced by local people's governments at or above the county level. The delimitation of areas prone to collapse, landslide, and debris flow shall be coordinated with the areas prone to geological disasters and key control areas determined in geological disaster prevention plans.

In areas with severe soil erosion and fragile ecology, production and construction activities that may cause soil erosion shall be restricted or prohibited, and plants, sand crust, crust, lichens, etc. shall be strictly protected.
On the slopes and banks of erosion gullies, on both sides of rivers, and around lakes and reservoirs, owners, users of land or relevant management units shall create plant protection belts. It is prohibited to reclaim or develop plant protection belts.

Owners or users of soil and water conservation facilities shall strengthen the management and maintenance of such facilities, implement maintenance responsibilities, and ensure their normal functioning.

It is prohibited to reclaim and plant crops on steep slopes with a gradient of 25 degrees or more. For planting economic forests on steep slopes with a gradient of 25 degrees or more, tree species shall be scientifically selected, the scale shall be reasonably determined, and soil and water conservation measures shall be taken to prevent soil erosion.
Provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, based on actual conditions in their respective administrative regions, stipulate a lower prohibited reclaiming gradient than 25 degrees. The scope of steep slopes where reclamation is prohibited shall be delimited and announced by the local county people's government.

It is prohibited to reclaim land by destroying forests or grasslands, and to collect Facai (a type of algae). It is prohibited to peel off turf, dig tree roots, or dig Cordyceps, licorice, ephedra, etc., excessively in key prevention areas and key control areas for soil erosion.

Forest logging shall adopt reasonable methods, and clear-cutting shall be strictly controlled; for protection forests such as water conservation forests, soil and water conservation forests, and windbreak and sand-fixing forests, only tending and regeneration logging shall be carried out; measures to prevent soil erosion shall be taken in logging areas and skidding roads, and timely reforestation shall be carried out after logging.
For logging in forest areas, the logging plan shall include soil and water conservation measures. After the logging plan is approved by the forestry department, the forestry department and the water administrative department shall supervise its implementation.

For afforestation, tending young forests, planting Chinese medicinal materials, etc., on slopes with a gradient of 5 degrees or more, soil and water conservation measures shall be taken.
For reclaiming and planting crops on barren slopes with a gradient below the prohibited reclaiming gradient but 5 degrees or more, soil and water conservation measures shall be taken. Specific measures shall be prescribed by provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government based on actual conditions in their respective administrative regions.

The site selection and route selection of production and construction projects shall avoid key prevention areas and key control areas for soil erosion; where avoidance is impossible, the prevention and control standards shall be improved, construction techniques shall be optimized, the scope of surface disturbance and vegetation damage shall be reduced, and potential soil erosion shall be effectively controlled.

When launching production and construction projects in mountainous, hilly, sandstorm areas, and other areas prone to soil erosion determined by soil and water conservation plans that may cause soil erosion, the construction unit shall prepare a soil and water conservation plan and submit it to the water administrative department of the people's government at or above the county level for approval, and shall adopt soil erosion prevention and control measures in accordance with the approved plan. If the unit lacks the capacity to prepare a plan, it shall entrust an institution with the corresponding technical conditions to prepare it.
A soil and water conservation plan shall include the scope, objectives, measures, and investment for soil erosion prevention and control.
If major changes occur in the location or scale of the production and construction project after the plan is approved, the plan shall be supplemented or revised and submitted to the original approving authority for approval. If major changes need to be made to the soil and water conservation measures during implementation, approval from the original approving authority shall be obtained.
The measures for preparing and approving soil and water conservation plans for production and construction projects shall be formulated by the water administrative department of the State Council.

For a production and construction project that is required by law to prepare a soil and water conservation plan, if the construction unit fails to prepare the plan or the plan has not been approved by the water administrative department, the project shall not commence construction.

The soil and water conservation facilities in a production and construction project that is required by law to prepare a soil and water conservation plan shall be designed, constructed, and put into operation simultaneously with the main project; upon completion and acceptance of the production and construction project, the soil and water conservation facilities shall be accepted; if the soil and water conservation facilities have not been accepted or fail the acceptance, the production and construction project shall not be put into operation.

For a production and construction project that is required by law to prepare a soil and water conservation plan, the sand, stone, soil, gangue, tailings, waste residues, etc., discharged during its production and construction activities shall be comprehensively utilized; if comprehensive utilization is impossible and disposal is indeed necessary, they shall be stacked in the designated storage sites determined in the soil and water conservation plan, and measures shall be taken to ensure that no new hazards are caused.

The water administrative departments of people's governments at or above the county level and river basin management agencies shall conduct follow-up inspections on the implementation of soil and water conservation plans for production and construction projects, and promptly address any problems discovered.

The State shall strengthen the construction of key soil and water conservation projects such as converting sloping farmland to terraced fields and silt retention dams in key prevention areas and key control areas for soil erosion, and increase ecological restoration efforts.
The water administrative departments of people's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen the construction management of key soil and water conservation projects, and establish and improve operation and maintenance management systems.

The State shall strengthen the prevention and control of soil erosion in river source areas, drinking water source protection areas, and water conservation areas, raise funds through multiple channels, and incorporate soil and water conservation ecological benefit compensation into the national ecological benefit compensation system.

If soil erosion is caused by launching a production and construction project or engaging in other production and construction activities, it shall be controlled.
For launching production and construction projects or engaging in other production and construction activities in mountainous, hilly, sandstorm areas, and other areas prone to soil erosion determined by soil and water conservation plans, which damage soil and water conservation facilities or landform vegetation and cannot restore the original soil and water conservation functions, a soil and water conservation compensation fee shall be paid, which shall be used exclusively for soil erosion prevention and control. The special soil erosion prevention and control shall be organized and implemented by the water administrative department. The measures for the collection and use management of soil and water conservation compensation fees shall be formulated by the finance department and the price department of the State Council jointly with the water administrative department of the State Council.
The soil and water conservation costs incurred during the construction and production processes of production and construction projects shall be handled in accordance with the unified financial accounting system of the State.

The State encourages units and individuals to participate in soil erosion control in accordance with soil and water conservation plans, and provides support in terms of funds, technology, taxation, etc.

The State encourages and supports the contracting of barren mountains, barren gullies, barren hills, and barren beaches for control, to prevent and control soil erosion, protect and improve the ecological environment, promote rational development and sustainable use of land resources, and protect the legitimate rights and interests of parties to land contracts according to law.
For contracts to control barren mountains, barren gullies, barren hills, barren beaches, and to contract rural land in areas with severe soil erosion, the land contract signed according to law shall include the responsibility for preventing and controlling soil erosion.

In water erosion areas, local people's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall organize units and individuals, taking small watersheds formed by natural gullies and their side slopes as units, to adopt engineering measures, plant measures, conservation tillage, etc., according to local conditions, to carry out comprehensive control of soil erosion on sloping farmland and gullies.
In wind erosion areas, local people's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall organize units and individuals, according to local conditions, to adopt measures such as rotational grazing enclosure, tree and grass planting, setting up artificial sand barriers and grid forest belts, to establish a windbreak and sand-fixing protection system.
In gravity erosion areas, local people's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall organize units and individuals to adopt measures such as monitoring, runoff drainage, slope cutting and load reduction, support and slope stabilization, construction of retaining works, to establish a monitoring, forecasting, and early warning system.

In drinking water source protection areas, local people's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall organize units and individuals to adopt measures such as prevention protection, natural restoration, and comprehensive control, build plant filter belts, actively promote biogas, carry out clean small watershed construction, strictly control the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides, reduce non-point source pollution caused by soil erosion, and protect drinking water sources.

Where crops have already been planted on steep slopes where reclamation is prohibited, the land shall be returned to forest or grass in accordance with relevant State regulations; if reclamation withdrawal is truly difficult due to cropland shortage, terraced fields shall be constructed or other soil and water conservation measures shall be taken.
For planting crops on sloping farmland with a gradient below the prohibited reclaiming gradient, measures such as building terraced fields, slope water system management, water and soil conservation tillage, or reclamation withdrawal shall be taken according to different situations.

The topsoil of land occupied by production and construction activities shall be stripped, preserved, and utilized in layers to achieve balance in earthwork excavation and backfilling, and reduce the scope of surface disturbance; for storage sites of discarded sand, stone, soil, gangue, tailings, waste residues, etc., measures such as retaining walls, slope protection, flood control and drainage shall be taken. After the production and construction activities are completed, trees and grass shall be promptly planted on the bare land of borrow pits, excavation faces, and storage sites to restore vegetation, and the closed tailings ponds shall be reclaimed.
For production and construction activities in arid and water-deficient areas, measures to prevent wind erosion shall be taken, precipitation storage and infiltration facilities shall be installed, and precipitation resources shall be fully utilized.

The water administrative departments of people's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen soil and water conservation monitoring work, and give full play to the role of soil and water conservation monitoring in government decision-making, economic and social development, and public services. People's governments at or above the county level shall ensure funding for soil and water conservation monitoring.
The water administrative department of the State Council shall improve the national soil and water conservation monitoring network and carry out dynamic monitoring of soil erosion nationwide.

For large and medium-sized production and construction projects that may cause severe soil erosion, the construction unit shall, on its own or by entrusting an institution qualified for soil and water conservation monitoring, monitor the soil erosion caused by the production and construction activities, and regularly report the monitoring situation to the local water administrative department.
Entities engaged in soil and water conservation monitoring activities shall comply with relevant national technical standards, specifications, and procedures to ensure monitoring quality.

The water administrative departments of people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for supervising and inspecting soil and water conservation conditions. River basin management agencies may exercise the supervision and inspection authority of the water administrative department of the State Council within their jurisdiction.

When performing supervision and inspection duties according to law, water law enforcement and supervision personnel shall show their law enforcement credentials. The unit or individual under inspection shall cooperate with the soil and water conservation supervision and inspection, truthfully report the situation, and provide relevant documents, permits, and materials; they shall not refuse or obstruct water law enforcement and supervision personnel from performing official duties.

Disputes over soil erosion between different administrative regions shall be resolved through consultation; if consultation fails, they shall be adjudicated by the common people's government at the next higher level.

Where the water administrative department or any other department exercising supervision and management authority pursuant to this Law fails to make an administrative licensing decision or handle approval documents according to law, fails to investigate upon discovering an illegal act or upon receiving a report of an illegal act, or commits any other act of failing to perform duties in accordance with this Law, the persons directly in charge and other directly responsible persons shall be given sanctions according to law.

In violation of the provisions of this Law, engaging in activities such as soil extraction, sand digging, and stone quarrying in areas prone to collapse, landslide, or debris flow that may cause soil erosion, the water administrative department of the local people's government at or above the county level shall order the cessation of the illegal act, confiscate the illegal gains, and impose a fine of not less than 1,000 yuan but not more than 10,000 yuan on an individual, and a fine of not less than 20,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan on a unit.

In violation of the provisions of this Law, reclaiming and planting crops on steep slopes with a gradient above the prohibited reclaiming gradient, or reclaiming or developing within plant protection belts where reclamation or development is prohibited, the water administrative department of the local people's government at or above the county level shall order the cessation of the illegal act and take remedial measures such as returning farmland to forest or restoring vegetation; according to the area reclaimed or developed, a fine of not more than 2 yuan per square meter may be imposed on an individual, and a fine of not more than 10 yuan per square meter on a unit.

In violation of the provisions of this Law, reclaiming land by destroying forests or grasslands, penalties shall be imposed in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Forest Law of the People's Republic of China and the Grassland Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 51 Anyone who, in violation of this Law, collects hair weeds, or removes turf, digs tree stumps, or indiscriminately digs Cordyceps sinensis, licorice, or ephedra, etc. in key prevention areas and key control areas of soil erosion, shall be ordered by the water administrative department of the local people's government at or above the county level to cease the illegal act, take remedial measures, confiscate the illegal gains, and concurrently be imposed a fine of not less than one time but not more than five times the illegal gains; if there are no illegal gains, a fine of not more than 50,000 yuan may be imposed.
Anyone who commits the illegal act as prescribed in the preceding paragraph in grassland areas shall be penalized in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Grassland Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 52 Anyone who, when felling trees in forest areas, fails to take measures to prevent soil erosion according to law, shall be ordered by the forestry department or the water administrative department of the local people's government at or above the county level to make corrections within a prescribed time limit and take remedial measures; if soil erosion is caused, the water administrative department shall impose a fine of not less than two yuan but not more than ten yuan per square meter based on the area of soil erosion.

Article 54 Anyone who, in violation of this Law, puts a production or construction project into operation or use without the soil and water conservation facilities having been inspected or having passed inspection, shall be ordered by the water administrative department of the people's government at or above the county level to cease production or use until the inspection is passed, and a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan shall be imposed.

Article 55 Anyone who, in violation of this Law, dumps sand, stone, soil, gangue, tailings, waste residue, etc. in areas other than the special storage sites designated in the soil and water conservation plan, shall be ordered by the water administrative department of the local people's government at or above the county level to cease the illegal act and clean up within a prescribed time limit, and a fine of not less than ten yuan but not more than twenty yuan per cubic meter based on the volume dumped shall be imposed; if the cleanup is not completed within the time limit, the water administrative department may designate a unit with cleanup capability to carry out the cleanup on its behalf, and the expenses incurred shall be borne by the violator.

Article 56 Anyone who, in violation of this Law, causes soil erosion by launching a production or construction project or engaging in other production and construction activities and fails to carry out treatment, shall be ordered by the water administrative department of the people's government at or above the county level to treat the soil erosion within a prescribed time limit; if treatment is still not carried out within the time limit, the water administrative department may designate a unit with treatment capability to carry out the treatment on its behalf, and the expenses incurred shall be borne by the violator.

Article 57 Anyone who, in violation of this Law, refuses to pay the soil and water conservation compensation fee, shall be ordered by the water administrative department of the people's government at or above the county level to pay within a prescribed time limit; if payment is not made within the time limit, a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the overdue amount shall be imposed from the date of default, and a fine of not more than three times the payable soil and water conservation compensation fee may be imposed.

Article 58 Anyone who, in violation of this Law, causes harm from soil erosion, shall bear civil liability according to law; if the act constitutes a violation of public security administration, the public security organ shall impose a public security penalty according to law; if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 59 The institution designated by the local people's government at or above the county level according to local conditions to be responsible for soil and water conservation work shall exercise the functions and duties of the water administrative department concerning soil and water conservation as prescribed in this Law.
Article 60 This Law shall come into force as of March 1, 2011.
